title: Elevated C-Reactive Protein and Subsequent Patient-Reported Cognitive Problems in Older Breast Cancer Survivors: The Thinking and Living With Cancer Study
notes: TLC study: large prospective national cohort, up to 60 months follow-up. Random effect-lagged fluctuation model. Between-person ln-CRP × survivor interaction → FACT-Cog Total: B=-3.43, SE=1.39, p=.014. Survivors with higher CRP had worse self-reported cognition; not seen in controls. FACT-Cog scores 9.5 and 14.2 points lower at CRP of 3.0 and 10.0 mg/L. Objective neuropsych (APE domain, LM domain) NOT significant for CRP interaction. Trails B trend only. Effects unchanged by depression or anxiety. Primary outcome: self-reported cognition (FACT-Cog). Covariates: age, race, site, WRAT4, obesity, comorbidities. Stage I=60.9%, ER+=87.6%. Only 23.3% received chemotherapy.
null_findings: APE (Attention/Processing Speed/Exec) domain: between-person CRP × group interaction p=.922
LM (Learning/Memory) domain: between-person CRP × group interaction p=.746
Within-person CRP fluctuations: no significant effect on any outcome
